h1: Winery licensing: the steps most places share
title: Winery Licensing: Common Steps | Craft Beer School
desc: The usual steps to licence a winery: company set-up, site approval, production and sale permits, label approval and duty registration. Check local rules.
teaser: Rules differ by country and by Indian state, but the order of work is similar. Plan licensing before you build.
standfirst: Licences decide when you can sell, so they shape the whole timeline. This guide covers the steps most places share and the questions to put to the regulator. It is not legal advice.
sections:
A winery that is built before its licence is secured can sit idle with a bill to pay. Approvals take time and some depend on the building being a certain way. Talk to the regulator or a licensing adviser before you buy land or sign a lease.

Alcohol is regulated in every country. In India it is a state subject, so the licence types, the process, the fees and the label rules differ by state and change. In other countries, rules differ by nation and often by region. This guide describes the common shape. It names no section numbers or fees because they vary and change.

Write your questions down before the first meeting. Which licences do I need to make, store, sell on site, sell wholesale and export? Which premises standards apply? What records must I keep? How long do approvals last and when must I renew? Written questions get written answers. Written answers are worth keeping.

Most regulators want a registered business: a company, partnership or other recognised form. Choose it with an accountant or lawyer, since it affects liability, tax and how investors can join. Register for the general business taxes that apply to you.

The site must usually fit local rules on land use, zoning, distance from schools or places of worship and similar restrictions. Check whether farmland can be used for a winery and what permits the building needs. Plans for the premises are often part of the licence application.

Look at water, effluent and waste as well. Wineries use a lot of water in cleaning and release wastewater with organic matter. Pollution control approvals may apply.

Ask the local authority for a written note on land use before you pay a deposit. Verbal comfort from a seller is not an approval.

A production licence lets you make wine. The regulator may inspect the premises and ask for plans, equipment lists, a description of the process and details of storage. Some places require a named responsible person or a set of records for every batch. Keep accurate production records from day one, because you will be asked for them.

Think about the layout. Regulators and inspectors often want clear separation of production, storage and any sale area, with secure storage for stock. Design the building with the licence in mind and ask for a view on your plans before construction.

Selling is often a separate permission from making. It can differ again for on-site sale, tastings, wholesale, retail, export and online. Some places require use of a licensed distributor. See getting wine into shops and restaurants. If you plan a tasting room, ask whether visitors may taste and buy on site.
Step five: duty, labels and food safety

Excise duty or tax on alcohol is common. You will usually have to register, keep stock records and pay on time. Labels usually need to state certain information and may need approval before use. Packaging rules may apply as well. Food safety registration is often needed for producers.

Check label rules before you print. A label rejected after printing is wasted money.

Records connect everything. Many regulators want to see what grapes or fruit came in, what wine was made, what was bottled, what was sold and what was lost. A simple batch sheet filled in as you work is far easier than rebuilding the story from memory at an audit.
Plan the timeline and the paperwork

Make a list of every permit, who issues it, what it needs, how long it has taken others and what it depends on. Build float into your timeline and your cash flow. See funding a winery.

We cannot promise that any licence will be granted. Your job is to apply carefully and keep the records. A licensing adviser or lawyer who knows your region can save months.

Keep a single folder, paper or digital, with every application, receipt, plan and letter. Renewals come around every year in many places. Missing one can halt sales. Put renewal dates in a calendar with a reminder well ahead.

If you work with a consultant on your project report, make licensing a line in the plan. See writing a project report for a winery.
faqs: How long does it take to get a winery licence?
It varies widely by place and by how complete your application is. Ask the regulator and others who have done it.
Do I need a licence to make wine for sale?
Yes, nearly everywhere. Making wine without a licence can carry serious penalties.
Is the licence the same in every Indian state?
No. Alcohol is a state subject and rules differ and change.
Do I need a separate licence for a tasting room?
Often yes, or additional conditions. Ask the regulator.
